newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador plans to slash spending - gov't advisor.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador plans to slash spending - gov't advisor.

text.p: The economic plan Ecuador will announce Friday will focus on streamlining the budget and improving tax collection, a government advisor said Thursday.

"The economic plan does not aim to create new taxes or raise rates for basic public services. It will be based only on spending cuts and the efficient use of Customs revenue," the advisor, who requested anonymity, told Reuters.
President Fabian Alarcon said Wednesday he would unveil his new government's economic plan on Friday.

The president, who heads an interim 18-month administration after Congress ousted former president Abdala Bucaram three weeks ago, said he would strive to plug the country's fiscal hole without a great social cost.
Ecuador faces a budget deficit estimated at between five and seven percent of gross domestic product this year.
"The government will not necessarily seek to wipe out the deficit, but to reduce it to 2.5 percent by the end of its mandate," the advisor said.
"We are not thinking of raising electricity or petrol prices, nor has the Central Bank mentioned the possibility of a devaluation, at least for the time being," he added.

However, he warned cutting state spending was "a wild card -- you don't know the outcome. If you don't succeed in reducing the fiscal gap and oil prices keep falling, then you will have to raise a basic utility tariff or hike petrol prices again."
